correctness.rationale: For the affine bracket [e1,e2]=e2, writing alpha=[[p,q],[r,s]] gives alpha([e1,e2])=[alpha(e1),alpha(e2)] iff q=0 and s(1-p)=0, valid over every field. The Yau bracket is s det(x,y)e2. Direct expansion of the Nijenhuis torsion for arbitrary N=[[a,b],[c,d]] cancels identically; hence the sole additional Nijenhuis requirement is [N,alpha]=0. The union of two affine planes in the alpha variables meets in a line, giving 2q^2-q twists; precisely alpha=0,I are scalar, with q^4 commuting N each. All other 2-by-2 alpha have degree-two minimal polynomial and centralizer Fq[alpha], of size q^2. Thus 4q^4-q^3-2q^2 pairs, with each extension field replacing q by q^m; exponentiating its counts gives (1-q^3 T)(1-q^2 T)^2/(1-q^4 T)^4. Independent full commutator enumeration at q=2,3,5 gave twist counts 6,15,45 and fiber distributions {q^4:2,q^2:2q^2-q-2}, respectively. The finite checks corroborate, not replace, the arbitrary-field proof.

value.rationale: The nonabelian 2D affine Lie algebra is the unique 2D nonabelian Lie algebra up to isomorphism; all Yau endomorphism twists, not an arbitrary slice, form a natural family. Exact exceptional scalar fibers, generic commuting-matrix fibers, and their all-extension arithmetic zeta determine the complete finite-field moduli distribution, a useful benchmark beyond a trivial single-matrix substitution.
